About Enduro Genetics

Enduro Genetics is a Copenhagen-based synthetic biology company commercializing Enduro Sense™, a genetic platform that increases the productivity of production hosts and cell lines in existing and new recombinant biomanufacturing processes. Enduro Sense™ links production to cellular fitness, so cells increase their production, stay productive over longer runs and at larger scale.

Enduro Sense™ has been deployed and demonstrated for more than 20 bioproducts, from industrial enzymes and food proteins to pharmaceutical peptides and biologics.

Why join us

In a 25-person company, your work will be visible and your results will shape how we grow. You will be part of our commercial team, working closely with leadership and our client delivery team. We offer a competitive salary package, including bonus. If you are results-driven and want to bring a proven new technology to biomanufacturers, we'd like to hear from you.

The role

You will lead market mapping, prospecting and lead qualification across biopharma, CDMOs and bioindustrial companies. You will identify the decision-makers, start conversations, assess technical and commercial fit, and advance promising opportunities with our client delivery team.

You'll join with the groundwork in place: an established CRM, market databases and sales tools, an active pipeline, and ongoing dialogues with prospective customers.

What you'll do

• Continued market mapping of applications, target companies and decision-makers to set prospecting priorities.

• Run outbound prospecting, and handle and prioritize incoming leads.

• Conduct initial discovery and pitch meetings, establishing customer needs, technical fit and next steps.

• Represent Enduro at conferences and events, and follow up with relevant contacts.

• Develop and tailor pitch decks, case studies and other customer-facing materials.

• Coordinate customer proposals with the client delivery team, including the customer-facing narrative, scope, deliverables and timelines.

What you bring

• A scientific background in biotechnology, molecular biology, bioprocessing or a related field, ideally at MSc or PhD level.

• Around 3–5 years of experience in business development, technical sales or another customer-facing role in biotechnology, biomanufacturing, CDMO services, genetics or similar platform technologies.

• Experience in selling, qualifying opportunities, presenting technical solutions and contributing to sales proposals.

• Outgoing, sound commercial judgement and a disciplined approach to sales. .

• Fluent English. Danish is an advantage.

Experience with microbial or CHO production systems, an established industry network or complex deal negotiations is a plus.

You're self-driven, curious about the science behind what you sell, and comfortable introducing a new approach to experienced technical audiences.

Practical details

• Location: Copenhagen, on-site

• Compensation: Competitive salary package, including bonus

• Travel: Expect travel for conferences and client visits.

Interested? Apply here https://EnduroGenetics.reqruiting.com/job.aspx?id=29680 . We review applications on a rolling basis.

Grow into Quality Assurance while helping us build the QA framework of tomorrow

Are you curious, structured, and good at connecting the dots?

Would you like to develop broad Quality Assurance competencies within clinical research rather than being placed in a narrow specialty from day one? And does the combination of quality, people, problem-solving, continuous improvement, and new technology sound exciting?

Then you might be the person we are looking for.

At Sanos, we are looking for an Associate QA Manager to join our Group Quality Assurance team and work closely with our QA Director and colleagues across the organization.

We do not expect you to know everything from day one. Instead, we are looking for someone with the curiosity, mindset, and drive to learn. You will gain exposure to Quality Assurance across a full-circle clinical research organization and gradually take on more responsibility as your competencies grow.

What makes this role different?

At Sanos, QA is not about creating bureaucracy or policing the organization.

Our approach is pragmatic and risk-based. We work closely with the business to support patient safety, data integrity, and regulatory compliance while designing processes that work in practice.

We are also on an AI and automation journey, exploring how technology can reduce repetitive work and allow us to focus on activities where human judgment and quality expertise create the most value.

This is an opportunity to help shape the QA framework of tomorrow while building a broad quality foundation for your own career.

What will you work with?

Depending on your development, interests, and the needs of the organization, you will gradually be involved in areas such as:

• Supporting and improving our Quality Management System (QMS)

• SOP development and document management

• Deviations, CAPAs, and quality investigations

• Quality metrics and continuous improvement activities

• Internal, supplier, and sponsor audits

• Inspection readiness and regulatory compliance

• Vendor qualification and oversight

• Supporting clinical sites on quality-related matters

• Validation and oversight of computerized systems

• Quality projects, process improvements, and digital initiatives

In short, you will help solve quality challenges, improve processes, and support colleagues across the organization.

Who are we looking for?

Your background may be within life sciences, health sciences, clinical research, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, or another regulated environment.

Previous QA experience is an advantage, but it is not what will determine whether you are the right fit. We are equally interested in candidates with the right mindset, curiosity, and motivation to develop within Quality Assurance.

We believe you will thrive in this role if you:

• Are curious and learn quickly

• Can connect the dots and solve problems independently

• Balance attention to detail with an understanding of the bigger picture

• Enjoy working with people and building relationships

• Have a pragmatic and risk-based mindset

• Like improving processes and ways of working

• Can manage multiple activities and create structure

• Are interested in technology, AI, and automation

• Take ownership and follow things through

• Bring a positive attitude and a good sense of humour

You must be able to communicate professionally in English, both orally and in writing. Danish language skills are important for collaboration with our Danish sites and colleagues.

Are we the right cultural fit?

Our commitment to you is encapsulated in our promise to every one of our employees saying, ‘Trust in you – in your development and impact’.

This pledge extends uniformly across all entities within the Sanos organization, ensuring that you feel its effects from the very outset of your interaction.

If you are curious about whether you would thrive within the Sanos culture and the Sanos way of leading, reflect on whether you see yourself working within our principles:

Take on - Responsibility is given, and we inspire you to take it

Try out - Explore diverse tasks and grow professionally

Team up - We don’t just work together; we thrive together

Want to know more? Check out the Voice of Sanos Group people here.

What can you expect from us?

A steep learning curve

You will gain exposure to a broad QA landscape across multiple disciplines and business areas.

Real mentorship

You will work closely with experienced QA professionals who will help you understand not only what we do, but why we do it.

Freedom with responsibility

As your experience grows, so will your ownership. We trust people to solve problems rather than prescribing every step.

Psychological safety

We encourage questions, open dialogue, and learning from mistakes.

Influence

You will help shape how QA continues to evolve at Sanos through continuous improvement, digitalization, and new ways of working.

Room to find your specialty

Whether your interests develop towards audits, quality systems, compliance, computerized systems, site quality, vendor quality, or something entirely different, we want to support your growth.

About Sanos

Sanos is a global multi-niche Clinical Research Organization (CRO) with full-circle clinical capabilities. We specialize in three main areas: Neurological Disorders (NeuroScios), Dermatological Conditions (Blueskin), and Musculoskeletal and Related Disorders (NBCD). Our core expertise lies in Science, Medical, and Clinical Operational functions.

Sanos is committed to delivering high-quality clinical trials and innovative solutions, supported by a robust organizational structure and a focus on specialization. Our brands include NBCD, Blueskin, NeuroScios, and Sanos Clinic.

The position is based primarily in Søborg, with flexibility for remote work. Collaboration with colleagues across Sanos locations is part of the role, and some travel between sites, as well as occasional international travel, should be expected.

Do you want to grow with us?

You do not need to tick every box before applying.

If you are curious about Quality Assurance, motivated by continuous learning, and excited by the opportunity to help shape the future of quality in clinical research, we would love to hear from you.

Application

We only accept applications submitted through the application link.

For further information about the role, please contact Emma Snefeldt, QA Director, at ESN@Sanos.com or +45 53 86 38 62.

We conduct interviews on an ongoing basis and will close the position when we find the right candidate.

We encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of ethnic background, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion, or age.

We value your privacy and handle personal data with care. Please see our privacy policy for applicants for further information.

Picture your typical week: on Monday you’re on-site at a client, driving a project team through a critical phase of an IT/OT implementation. By Wednesday you’re facilitating a workshop across business, IT, and engineering to resolve a key delivery issue. Friday, you’re back at Emendo’s Nordhavn office sharing what you learned and sharpening the methods your colleagues will use on their projects. If that sounds like work you’d love, keep reading.

Why We’re Hiring Now

We paused hiring over the past year to be deliberate about the team we build next. The consulting market in Denmark has tightened, and our clients have changed how they buy: they want consultants who can take real ownership, navigate complexity, and show measurable progress quickly. We are now making a small number of hires — each one matters, and we are taking the time to find the right people.

About Emendo

Emendo is a 200-person consultancy built by people who used to sit on the client side — running transformation programmes inside leading global companies before deciding to do it for a living. We understand the pressure a site director feels before a go-live, we know what an inspector looks for in a regulated environment, and we speak the language of the people who operate the systems we implement. We work across the full Operational value chain from R&D through shipping, with offices in Copenhagen, Kalundborg, Odense, Silkeborg, Munich, and Raleigh (USA). Our strategy is simple: deliver faster, prove value in hard numbers, and use our methods and AI tools to do what we do well — only quicker.

We are a methods-driven firm rooted in operational excellence and Lean. Our motto, Observe, Think, Improve, is itself a method: go to the floor, understand what is actually happening, analyse it rigorously, then design and implement a concrete improvement. That simplicity is what makes it reliable when the project gets complicated and the usual playbooks stop working.

The Role

You will lead projects and workstreams within IT/OT transformation engagements for our clients, mainly in (but not limited to) pharma and regulated industries— operating at the intersection of technology, business process, and organisational change. You are expected to create structure, drive progress, coordinate stakeholders, and make sure decisions turn into action. At Emendo, being a Lead Consultant means taking real ownership while continuing to build the judgement and client credibility required to lead increasingly complex engagements.

What You Will Do

• Lead projects and workstreams on-site, driving IT/OT implementations across enterprise, operations management, process control, and process equipment layers

• Create structure and momentum through clear planning, governance, stakeholder alignment, and follow-up

• Drive measurable progress in short cycles — turning project activity into tangible outcomes

• Coordinate cross-functional teams across business, IT, engineering, vendors, and other stakeholders

• Facilitate workshops, resolve issues, manage dependencies, and turn complex discussions into clear decisions and actions

• Engage with solution architecture, validation concepts, and implementation planning within complex project environments

• Build strong client relationships and become a trusted counterpart who takes ownership and gets things done

• Apply Observe, Think, Improve as your foundation and contribute to strengthening Emendo’s methods and tools

What It Takes

Must-Have Qualifications

• Master’s degree in engineering, IT, business, innovation, or a related discipline

• 2–5+ years of hands-on experience delivering IT/OT projects, digital transformations, or technology implementations — ideally within pharma or another regulated industry

• Experience taking ownership of a project, workstream, or significant delivery area

• Strong project management fundamentals, including planning, governance, risk and issue management, and stakeholder coordination

• Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to create structure in complex or changing environments

• Confidence working across business and technical stakeholders

• Fluent English, both written and spoken; Danish skills are strongly preferred, or a commitment to learn

• Willingness to work on-site at client locations in Denmark and occasionally internationally

Nice to have — but not required

None of the following are dealbreakers. If you tick even one or two, it tells us you will ramp up faster — but we have seen great consultants arrive without any of them and build the expertise here.

• Experience with GxP compliance, computer system validation (CSV/CSA), or regulatory frameworks in life sciences

• Familiarity with enterprise systems such as ERP or MES, process control, automation, or IT–OT integration

• Background in operational excellence, Lean, or continuous improvement methodologies

• Experience working across multiple sites or geographies in larger transformation programmes

• Familiarity with AI or automation tools applied to project delivery or enterprise transformation

What Makes Emendo Different

• Measured on outcomes, not utilisation — you work directly with industry leaders on engagements that matter

• Real responsibility early — with experienced colleagues around you when the challenge requires it

• One integrated firm with deep methods: cross-unit collaboration across Implementation, Engineering, Digital, and R&D, backed by a Lean toolbox and AI accelerators

• Freedom under responsibility — challenging projects with room to shape the solution and your own career

• A flat culture where your input matters and your wins are celebrated

• Competitive compensation reflecting the responsibility and impact expected in this role

This role is probably not for you if:

• You prefer purely advisory work with limited implementation responsibility.

• You work best with narrow ownership and very clear boundaries.

• You have strong technical exposure but limited experience driving cross-functional delivery.

Ready to Make an Impact?

We are hiring a small number of Lead Consultants this year. You will join a team that has led some of the largest IT/OT programmes in US and European companies — people who chose Emendo because they wanted meaningful responsibility in a firm that still feels personal. If that resonates, we’d like to hear from you.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. We will be in touch promptly.

For further information, reach out to Mikael Elley (me@emendo.com or +45 24 83 62 01).

Want to build technology that can help make heavy industry a little greener?

At Ammisorb, you won’t just be sitting behind a screen designing concepts. You’ll help build, test and improve the actual hardware behind a new way of recovering ammonia more efficiently.

We’re a DTU spinout working on technology that can support smaller, more flexible green ammonia systems, and we’re looking for a Development Engineer who wants real ownership from day one.

Your designs will be built. Tested. Challenged. Improved. And ultimately put into the field.

**About Ammisorb

**We develop sorption-based technology for separating and recovering ammonia more efficiently. Our Sorption Booster captures ammonia in solid sorbents and releases it in a controlled way for recovery as a concentrated product. It achieves 99% ammonia extraction (vs. <70% for conventional chillers) at below 50 bar. The technology targets lower-pressure ammonia production, helping make smaller and more flexible green ammonia systems possible. Find more info on our webpage: https://www.ammisorb.com/

**Role Purpose

**The Development Engineer will lead the design, development, assembly, integration, and testing of next-generation Sorption Booster systems. The role combines practical engineering work with system development activities, including mechanical and process design, component selection, prototype integration, troubleshooting, and coordination with internal and external stakeholders.

**Main Responsibilities

**

• 
Drive the design and development of next-generation Sorption Booster systems and absorber units based on experimental data obtained from previous prototype generations

• 
Lead mechanical and process design of ammonia sorption systems, including P&IDs, piping layouts, heat integration, component integration, and subsystem development

• 
Prepare CAD models, technical drawings, bills of materials (BOMs), and engineering documentation

• 
Take ownership of assembly, integration, and troubleshooting of experimental setups and prototype systems

• 
Identify, evaluate, and procure suitable components and equipment for prototype and pilot-scale systems

• 
Coordinate technical implementation with automation and control engineers

• 
Support field testing activities and collaboration with external partners and suppliers

• 
Lead safety assessments and implementation of safe engineering practices during system design and operation

• 
Independently propose and develop technical solutions for assigned subsystems and engineering challenges

• 
Support project coordination activities related to prototype development and testing

**Desired Profile and Competencies

**

• 
MSc or BSc in mechanical engineering, process engineering, energy engineering, or related field

• 
2–5 years of experience designing and building process or thermal equipment in R&D or industry

• 
Experience with 3D CAD (e.g. SolidWorks / Inventor) and practical engineering design

• 
Hands-on experience with mechanical assembly, piping, workshop activities, and experimental systems

• 
Experience with prototype or pilot-scale systems is considered an advantage

• 
Experience working with safety-critical laboratory setups and pressurized process equipment (e.g. HAZOP/risk assessment, PED, ATEX, hazardous gas handling) is considered an advantage

**What We Offer

**

• 
Real ownership of core hardware at an early stage – your designs go into the field

• 
A close-knit team rooted in DTU’s research environment, supported by advisors with industrial ammonia and hardware experience

• 
The chance to help shape an early-stage climate-tech company as it grows

• 
Competitive salary

Do you want a broad accounting role with significant responsibility and excellent development opportunities?

If you are an experienced accounting professional who enjoys taking ownership, working independently, and being part of a collaborative team, this could be exactly the opportunity you have been looking for.

At Gubra, we are experiencing continued growth and development. As our business expands, so do the opportunities for our employees to develop professionally and take on increasing responsibility. We are therefore looking for a Financial Accountant to join our Finance team and contribute to maintaining a high level of quality, compliance, and operational excellence across our group companies.

In this role, you will become part of our finance function where teamwork, trust, and continuous improvement are highly valued.

A broad accounting role with responsibility across multiple areas

As Financial Accountant, you will be responsible for a variety of accounting and controlling activities spanning day-to-day bookkeeping, reconciliations, month-end closing activities, reporting support, and audit preparation.

You will have ownership of your own areas while working closely with your colleagues in Finance. We take pride in supporting one another and working together to ensure successful month-end closings, reporting deadlines, audits, and daily operations.

Your primary responsibilities will include:

• Managing accounts receivable, including invoicing, cash registrations, reminders, and communication with customers' finance departments

• Maintaining and managing the fixed asset register, including verification of physical assets and correct accounting treatment

• Handling lease accounting in accordance with IFRS 16

• Performing foreign currency revaluations on currency accounts

• Acting as system owner for Corpay, PLEO, and e-conomic

• Preparing statutory and regulatory reporting, including submissions to Statistics Denmark and other authorities

• Supporting colleagues with accounting- and finance-related questions

• Participating in month-end closing activities, reconciliations, and audit preparation

• Contributing to process improvements, internal controls, and finance-related projects

• Supporting ad hoc tasks across the group's legal entities

As you grow in the role, you will have the opportunity to expand your responsibilities and actively influence how we develop our finance processes and controls.

An experienced accounting professional with a proactive mindset

Naturally, we are looking for someone with the right professional qualifications. However, your approach to work and collaboration is equally important.

We are looking for someone who takes ownership, follows through on commitments, and enjoys working in an environment that combines structured routines with changing priorities and deadlines.

In addition, you bring:

• You likely have 5+ years of experience from a finance function where you have worked independently with bookkeeping, reconciliations, month-end closing, and financial controls.

• Strong Excel skills and experience with financial systems

• A structured and detail-oriented approach to your work

• The ability to work independently and take responsibility for your areas

• A positive and collaborative mindset with a willingness to support colleagues across the organization

• Professional communication skills in both Danish and English, written and spoken

Experience from an international company with entities in multiple countries is considered an advantage, but not a requirement. Likewise, experience with Corpay, PLEO, and/or e-conomic is beneficial but not essential.

We are particularly interested in someone who is curious and analytical. You notice when something does not look right, investigate the underlying cause, and work proactively to find a solution rather than simply reporting the deviation.

Your new team

You will join a Finance team consisting of four colleagues, including yourself. We work closely together, share knowledge, and support one another in delivering high-quality financial operations.

The role can be structured as either a full-time or part-time position (32-37 hours per week), depending on your preferences and qualifications.

We look forward to welcoming a colleague who enjoys being part of a team while maintaining ownership of their own responsibilities.

What we offer

• A broad and independent role in a collaborative Finance team

• A full-time or part-time position (32-37 hours per week)

• Real responsibility and ownership from day one

• The opportunity to influence processes, workflows, and internal controls

• Flexible working arrangements, including the possibility of working from home

• Ongoing opportunities to develop your role and responsibilities

• An informal and positive working environment

• Dedicated colleagues and a strong team spirit

• Competitive salary based on qualifications

• Pension scheme and health insurance

• Start date as soon as possible, although we are happy to wait for the right candidate

About Gubra

Gubra is a disease-agnostic techbio company specialized in peptide-based drug discovery and development as well as preclinical contract research services striving for excellence at all levels. We insist on doing things efficiently - and often differently - to reach the results we aim for. Our vision is to become leaders in the path towards a more sustainable and healthier world. We do that by facilitating the discovery of new medicine, and by acting and inspiring others to fight the ongoing climate and biodiversity crises.

Gubra’s activities are focused on the early stages of drug development and are organised in two main highly synergistic business areas: Biotech and CRO Services. We generate our revenue by performing research for life science companies as well as by partnering projects from our discovery and development pipeline.

Our therapeutic focus is within metabolic and fibrotic diseases, and we specialize in in vivo pharmacology, ex vivo assays, drug profiling, histology, stereology and whole brain and organ imaging. In addition, we offer a full palette of advanced transcriptomics. Our ML/AI-driven peptide drug discovery platform streaMLine enables us to rapidly develop a peptide hit into a non-clinical candidate ready for development. Through a constant focus on high quality, scientific excellence, speed, and solid teamwork we have established ourselves as a highly professional and competent partner in the market.

People are our greatest asset, and our team consists of around 320 employees of which many are located in Hørsholm, Denmark. The mix of people from different cultures and educational backgrounds combined with our entrepreneurial mindset have greatly impacted our working environment, which is characterized by entrepreneurial drive, scientific curiosity, and teamwork – we join forces!

As our next Data Engineer – Data Insights & Analytics you will contribute to solving meaningful challenges across the life sciences industry. We offer specialised management consulting services, working with top-tier life sciences companies as well as biotech startups — locally and globally. From strategy development to hands-on implementation, we support our clients were impact matters most.

About the role

We seek a skilled and motivated Data Engineer to join our Data Insights & Analytics team. In this role, you will be responsible for designing, developing, automating, and maintaining robust data pipelines to ensure efficient data collection, storage, transformation, and processing. You will work closely with business analysts, cross-functional teams, and domain experts in the pharmaceutical industry to ensure that the data architecture supports advanced analytics and business intelligence across a range of pharmaceutical projects.

As a Data Engineer, your responsibilities include

• Build, implement, and automate efficient data ingestion pipelines that integrate data from diverse sources, including structured, semi-structured, and unstructured formats, while applying necessary business logic and transformations.

• Develop and maintain data processing solutions using technologies such as Azure Databricks, Azure Data Factory, SQL, Python, and PySpark.

• Apply data quality practices and frameworks to minimize anomalies and ensure the production of high-quality, reliable data for downstream systems.

• Incorporate error handling, exception management, monitoring, and auditing mechanisms to maintain end-to-end data traceability and support data lineage.

• Design and execute end-to-end tests to ensure the data pipeline and solutions are functioning as expected, covering a variety of data scenarios and ensuring that data flows accurately and reliably from source to target.

• Work closely with cross-functional teams, including data privacy officers, business analysts, and quality assurance teams, to ensure alignment with organizational goals and to facilitate seamless data integration and usage.

Required Skills and Qualifications

Educational background: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field.

Experience:

• Minimum of 2 years of hands-on experience in a Data Engineer role, with a focus on medium to complex data engineering projects, preferably in the pharmaceutical domain.

• Minimum of 2 years of hands-on experience in cloud data transformation platforms such as Azure Databricks, AWS, or GCP; relevant certifications are a plus.

• Minimum of 2 years of hands-on experience in Python or equivalent scripting languages is a must.

Technical Expertise:

• Proficient in Structured Query Language (SQL) and experienced in working with relational databases and cloud-based data platforms.

• Experience with Microsoft Azure data services and Databricks, including technologies such as Azure Data Factory, Azure Data Lake Storage, Delta Lake, Python, and PySpark.

• Experience with ETL/ELT processes, data ingestion, transformation, incremental processing, and data quality practices.

• Experience in data modeling and layered data architectures, including Medallion architecture and dimensional modeling concepts.

• Familiarity with RESTful APIs, Git, DevOps practices, and CI/CD processes is a plus.

• Good understanding of Veeva, Salesforce, IQVIA data models and data sources across HR and Sales functions.

• Familiarity with data visualization and analytics tools such as Power BI, Tableau, and Qlik is essential.

Soft-skills:

• Strong consulting mindset with the ability to work independently on defined tasks and collaborate effectively within medium to large-scale project teams.

• Proven ability to work in dynamic, fast-paced project environments without compromising on quality.

• Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting abilities.

Who is BASE life science?

Founded in 2015, BASE life science is a business and technology consulting company working exclusively in life sciences, built on a simple purpose: grow our people, and deliver real impact for our customers.

We don't think AI is a feature you bolt onto existing systems — we think it's the layer through which a life sciences company's strategy actually gets executed, end to end. Most of the industry is still proving AI can do one task at a time, function by function, pilot by pilot. We're building toward something bigger: AI that runs across clinical, regulatory, quality, and commercial work instead of stopping at the edges of a single application.

With headquarters in Denmark and offices across Spain, Switzerland, the UK, Germany, France, Italy, and the US, we work with top-10 pharma and ambitious biotechs alike, and with technology partners including Veeva, Salesforce, IQVIA, Google, AWS, Microsoft, and Amass — turning that belief into deployed, compliant, sellable solutions, not slideware.

Why join BASE life science?

At BASE, you work on meaningful, complex challenges at the intersection of technology, science, and business. We trust our people with real responsibility and support them in turning ambition into impact — grounded in five core values: team spirit, trust, openness, ambition, and execution.

• Ambition, encouraged through ownership and continuous learning.

• Execution — we focus on delivering solutions that work in practice.

• Openness — your ideas are heard, challenged constructively, and supported as you grow.

• Flexible ways of working, built on trust, autonomy, and balance.

• The opportunity to shape a practice, not just staff one.

Alongside this, we offer:

• Support for health and wellbeing, covering physical, mental, and social needs

• Flexible ways of working, built on trust, autonomy, and balance

• Ongoing learning and professional development throughout your career

• A modern work setup, with the tools and equipment needed to do great work

• Recognition of performance and impact, linked to contribution and results

• The opportunity to work on challenges that make a meaningful difference for patients and healthcare systems worldwide

Explore our work, values, and people at www.baselifescience.com

Interested?

If you find this position intriguing, don't delay—submit your application in English at your earliest convenience. We are continuously reviewing and assessing all incoming candidates and eagerly await your application.

At BASE life science, we value diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. Employment decisions are based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs

Scientific data engineer

Orbis is growing fast. As our biology and chemistry teams grow, we need our data infrastructure to scale as well. We are looking for a Scientific Data Engineer to build systems and structures that capture data accurately and smoothly so that the science team can focus on the science. You’ll work closely with biology, chemistry, design and data science teams to understand how they work and what they need from their data, identify areas for improvement and then build solutions using both commercial and custom tools.

This is a chance to join a growing biotech company at a crucial moment as we invest in our lab and data infrastructure, helping build a cutting-edge data platform, designing workflows and building pipelines.

This role would suit someone who loves data and code. Someone with a chemistry or biology background with a computational focus, or a software engineer with experience working in a scientific environment.

You will be working onsite in Copenhagen.

Responsibilities:

·      Develop and manage the Orbis data platform, spanning commercial software and custom solutions,

including implementing new systems and migrating existing data

·      Work with chemistry, biology and data science teams to gather requirements, prototype solutions, and

harmonise data operations across the organisation

·      Write and maintain ETL data pipelines to streamline data ingestion and organisation

·      Safeguard data integrity and quality in line with FAIR principles

·      Collaborate with software engineers and data scientists to enable AI&ML operations

·      Act as the go-to contact for lab scientists using our data products and infrastructure

Qualifications & experience

·      A degree in chemistry, biology, bioinformatics or a related field

·      A strong passion for data in drug discovery

·      3+ years of industry experience in a scientific environment, with hands-on exposure to drug discovery

data and how it flows from design through synthesis and testing

·      Good working knowledge of Python and common data libraries

·      Experience with relational databases and SQL

·      Experience designing data structures for scientific data

·      Strong communication skills and a track record of working collaboratively with scientists

Nice to have

·      Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS or GCP)

·      Software engineering practices such as Git, CI/CD, Docker and code testing

·      Experience with ELN or LIMS systems (e.g. Dotmatics, CDD Vault, Revvity Signals)

Application

Please contact Talent Acquisition Partner Mia Danielsen (part of

DEDENROTH) if you have any questions about the role or the process.

Phone: +45 26178142 /

Email: mia.danielsen@orbismedicines.com

oasicare is looking for an entrepreneurial senior commercial lead to take our women’s health medical device from early clinical adoption to scalable commercial growth.

We are a Danish medtech company developing solutions to improve outcomes in vaginal birth. Our first product, ASISU, is a CE-marked medical device designed to reduce the risk of perineal tears during childbirth. We are already working with leading maternity wards and clinical partners and are now entering the next phase: turning clinical traction into hospital-wide adoption, commercial partnerships, and international growth.

The role

As senior commercial lead, you will own oasicare’s commercial strategy, market development, revenue delivery and commercial organisation.

Your initial mandate is to determine how the existing distributor, direct-to-hospital and consumer-driven opportunities should be combined and sequenced by market. You will then lead execution of the optimal strategy.

You will personally own critical customers, hospitals and distributor relationships, early commercial experiments and major negotiations while building the team and systems required for scale.

Subject to performance, company development and achievement of agreed commercial milestones, the role has the potential to develop into the position of Chief Commercial Officer following a structured evaluation, expected within 9–12 months.

Lead hospital and market adoption

• Build relationships with maternity wards, clinicians, hospital management, procurement teams and relevant professional organisations.

• Convert clinical interest into agreed implementation pathways, trained users, product availability, utilisation and recurring orders.

• Define the role hospitals play in each go-to-market model: customer, clinical adopter, service provider, access partner or demand enabler.

• Personally lead strategically important early accounts and partnerships.

Advance and activate a suitable distributor strategy

• Validate partner fit, commitment, commercial terms, evidence expectations, country access and launch capabilities.

• Negotiate, appoint, onboard and manage distributors in markets where this is the preferred route.

• Establish country plans, training, marketing support, order commitments and performance expectations.

• Measure partner performance through hospital access, activation, sales-through and adoption, not only distributor purchases.

Advance and activate consumer-funded, hospital-enabled model

• Design and test the end-to-end journey from consumer awareness and purchase to hospital acceptance and clinical use.

• Validate willingness to pay, pricing, acquisition cost, conversion, contribution margin, fulfilment and customer support.

jobs.employer_name: Novo Nordisk Clinical Innovation Centre A/S
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

Contribute to early-phase clinical research and phase I trials at CLINiC. As a Clinical Research Physician, you will combine clinical work with medical and scientific knowledge across trial setup and execution. Your expertise will support participant safety, robust decision-making and reliable data generation, while contributing to the development of potential new treatments in line with the Novo R&D strategy.

Introduction

Novo Nordisk Clinical Innovation Centre A/S (CLINiC) is an organisation dedicated to early-phase clinical trials assessing the safety and tolerability, pharmaco-kinetics and dynamics of potential new Novo medicines. In this role, you will combine hands-on clinical activities, medical oversight and trial leadership in an environment where participant safety, scientific quality and operational excellence are central.

What you’ll bring

We are looking for a physician with strong clinical judgement, experience in clinical research and a collaborative approach.

• A Medical Doctor (MD) degree and solid clinical experience; a PhD is an advantage.

• Experience in conducting clinical trials as a Principal Investigator or Sub-Investigator; experience with early-phase clinical trials is an advantage.

• Knowledge of ICH-GCP and relevant regulatory frameworks.

• Solid experience in managing acute medical emergencies.

• Strong collaboration, stakeholder management, communication and presentation skills in an international setting.

• Fluency in Danish for interaction with trial participants and strong English skills for internal collaboration.

You bring a proactive, quality-focused mindset and can navigate complexity while keeping participant safety and trial excellence at the center of your decisions.

What you’ll do

You will play a key role in delivering safe, high-quality early-phase clinical trials at CLINiC. Your essential work will include:

• Leading and conducting clinical trials, including protocol review, trial execution, medical oversight and informal leadership of trial teams.

• Acting as Principal Investigator or Sub-Investigator, with responsibility for participant safety, trial conduct and data integrity.

• Conducting screening, in-house, overnight and ambulatory visits. Shift work (on-call or on-site) will be part of the role according to trial activities.

• Providing medical and scientific expertise to stakeholders and supporting the training and development of colleagues.

• Driving risk assessments, management of protocol deviations and quality processes.

• Contributing actively to cross-functional initiatives, continuous improvement and the development of supporting IT systems.

Who you’ll work with

You will join CLINiC in Gentofte as part of our Operations team, working closely across clinical, scientific and operational disciplines to deliver high-quality data to the Sponsor organisation. You will also support colleagues through medical guidance, knowledge sharing and informal leadership of trial teams.

What you can expect here

At CLINiC, you can expect meaningful clinical work in a highly collaborative environment. You will contribute to an organisation focused on participant safety, scientific excellence and continuous improvement, with opportunities to develop through cross-functional collaboration.

Salary: The annual base salary for this role ranges from DKK 847,000 to DKK 1,245,100, corresponding to the level of the position. Placement within the range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area, and relevant market benchmarks. Benefits are designed with different career and life stages in mind.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy: https://www.novonordisk.com/careers/working-at-novo-nordisk/total-rewards-benefits.html

Start now

Apply now and bring your clinical expertise to work that can shape the earliest stages of medicine development.

Application deadline: 25. October 2026

About the job

Group Internal Audit (GIA) in Saxo is responsible for carrying out risk-based operational audits across the organisation. Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the team helps to ensure that Saxo effectively manages and mitigates the risks associated with its business activities.

We are looking for an IT Audit Manager for our team covering IT Audits across Saxo. As an IT Audit Manager within Saxo, your tasks will include auditing, analysing, and assessing IT processes within Saxo’s IT architecture, system development, operations, and security.

“This is a great opportunity to set the direction for and lead IT audits in a dynamic organisation” – Sune Andreas Yung Nielsen, Head of IT Audit.

Responsibilities

• Establish best practice audit programs for validating IT processes and controls

• Carry out audits to identify shortcomings and provide assurance on established controls

• Develop recommendations to strengthen controls and address any residual risks

• Follow up on recommendations and re-assess whether solutions are adequate

Your profile

You are known for your professionalism, integrity, and trustworthiness. You are a curious, collaborative, and outgoing person, who thrives in diverse environments.

You are comfortable communicating with management and taking the lead, and, when necessary, you are willing to challenge the status quo.

While you have great attention to detail, you still manage to maintain an overview, see through complexity, and summarise issues clearly. What matters most to us, is that you are a team player at heart, with a flexible mindset, and dare to let your personality show. You see a direct link between your own success and the overall results of GIA.

You have knowledge and hands-on experience in the following areas:

• IT Governance

• IT Risk Management

• Software Development Life Cycle

• Cyber Security

• Data Analytics

You may already have or are interested in obtaining certifications such as CISA, CISM, or CISSP.

Proficiency in English, both verbal and written.

Would you like to lead the development of the frameworks that form the foundation of Saxo’s approach to preventing financial crime?

About the job

We are looking for an experienced leader to head our GWRA & Policies team within Financial Crime Prevention. You will lead the development and continuous enhancement of our Group-Wide Risk Assessment (GWRA) and financial crime policy frameworks, ensuring they remain robust, risk-based and aligned with evolving regulatory expectations.

As Head of FCP GWRA & Policies, you will lead a team of skilled specialists and provide direction on priorities, governance, and strategic initiatives. You will work closely with senior stakeholders across Compliance, Risk, Legal and the business, helping translate complex regulatory requirements into practical, scalable and sustainable solutions that support both compliance and business objectives.

This is a highly visible leadership role with significant influence across the organisation and a direct impact on Saxo's financial crime risk management framework.

Responsibilities

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Lead and develop the GWRA & Policies team, fostering a high-performing culture built on ownership, collaboration and continuous improvement.

• Set the strategic direction for Saxo's Group-Wide Risk Assessment framework, methodology and governance, ensuring it continues to evolve in line with emerging risks and regulatory expectations.

• Oversee the execution of the annual and ongoing enterprise-wide financial crime risk assessment process, including governance, stakeholder engagement, reporting and remediation activities.

• Drive the continuous development of Saxo's financial crime policy framework, ensuring policies are risk-based, practical and consistently implemented across the organisation.

• Monitor regulatory developments and emerging industry practices, translating complex requirements into clear frameworks, policies and guidance.

• Lead remediation and enhancement initiatives arising from audits, regulatory reviews and internal assessments, ensuring sustainable and timely outcomes.

• Act as a trusted advisor to senior management and governance forums on matters relating to financial crime risk, policy and regulatory expectations.

• Strengthen collaboration across Financial Crime Prevention, Compliance, Risk, Legal and local business units to ensure a coordinated approach to managing financial crime risk.

Your profile

You bring strong leadership experience and deep expertise in financial crime prevention, risk management or compliance. You combine strategic thinking with strong execution capabilities and have successfully led and developed specialist teams in complex environments.

You are comfortable operating in a complex and highly regulated environment, balancing regulatory expectations, risk considerations and business objectives. You build trusted relationships through your expertise, sound judgement and ability to engage stakeholders across the organisation.

You are comfortable discussing detailed risk assessment methodologies as well as advising senior management on strategic risk decisions, and you can translate complexity into clear direction and practical solutions.

We expect that you bring

• Extensive experience within Financial Crime Prevention, Compliance, Risk Management or a comparable regulatory function within banking or financial services.

• Strong expertise in AML, CTF, sanctions and broader financial crime risk management frameworks.

• Significant experience leading experienced specialists and developing high-performing teams.

• Proven experience designing, implementing and evolving enterprise-wide risk assessment methodologies and governance frameworks.

• Deep understanding of financial crime policy development and regulatory expectations across multiple jurisdictions.

• Demonstrated ability to engage and influence senior stakeholders, governance committees and executive management.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, combined with excellent written and verbal communication abilities.

• Experience operating in an international and matrix-based organisation.

• Fluent English, both written and spoken.

If you are motivated by leading experts, shaping enterprise-wide financial crime frameworks and influencing how a global organisation manages financial crime risk, we would love to hear from you.

We review applications and conduct interviews on an ongoing basis and encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

About the Job:

Join our team as a passionate and experienced Cyber Security Analyst to help safeguard our digital assets. In this role, you will focus on alert triage, incident response, and enhancing our Security Operations Centre (SOC).

Our multinational team leverages a diverse array of security tools, offering you a dynamic environment for learning and growth. We collaborate to investigate in-depth, with a goal to keep Saxo safe from external threats targeting our environments. You will become part of our ongoing efforts to enhance our forensic capabilities and leverage SOAR to automate triage workflows and improve detections.

Key Responsibilities:

In this role, you will be responsible for monitoring and triaging security alerts to keep our defences sharp. Additionally, you will get the opportunity to lead and conduct forensic investigations to uncover, understand and mitigate threats. Collaboration is key, as you will work closely with team members, our threat intelligence and Insider Threat team, Saxo organizational stakeholders, and external security partners to strengthen our security posture.

Further;

• Build and maintain operational awareness through trend analysis, dashboards, and reports for the C-suite.

• Mentor team members and conduct knowledge-sharing sessions to foster a culture of continuous improvement.

• Provide input to automation, enhancing detections, playbooks, and our security technology stack.

• Monitor, perform, and improve security controls to ensure robust protection.

• Investigative and triage assistance to our Insider Threat team

Your Profile:

You should have over 5 years of experience in the cybersecurity domain, demonstrating a proactive and diligent work ethic with an eye for detail. Your approach to tasks is marked by curiosity, creativity, and structure. Proficiency in one or more areas of cybersecurity forensics, such as binary triage, network log analysis, host forensics, and/or threat intelligence, is essential.

Experience with SIEM/SOAR platforms, endpoint security platforms, AI-enabled investigations, and ServiceNow or other ticketing platforms is required. Additionally, familiarity with SOAR playbooks, automation, and alert fine-tuning is a plus. Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, or SANS are advantageous.

About the role

As a Senior Observability Engineer at Saxo, you will join a specialised team responsible for the bank's observability platforms. We build and continuously improve solutions that provide visibility into the performance, stability, and health of critical business systems across our hybrid infrastructure.

You will help shape the future of Saxo's observability landscape by designing and operating solutions for metrics, logs, traces, and events across cloud and on-premises environments. Your work will enable engineering teams to better understand, monitor, and improve the systems that power Saxo.

Team perspective

"We are the eyes and ears of Saxo Bank's platform health. Our work is critical to maintaining stable and continuous operations across the organisation.

Our team is based in Denmark and India and consists of five specialists. While supporting our current platforms, we are also executing our roadmap for the next generation of observability capabilities."

Responsibilities

• Own and support the day-to-day operation of Saxo's observability platform.

• Partner closely with engineering teams to deliver meaningful monitoring and visibility across business-critical systems.

• Drive priorities, technical direction, and platform improvements within the team.

• Act as the observability platform architect, ensuring scalability, reliability, and long-term maintainability.

• Play a key role in delivering the next generation of Saxo's observability platform in collaboration with Enterprise Architecture, platform teams, and business stakeholders.

What success looks like

• Build expertise across our observability ecosystem, including Elastic, Grafana, Kibana, Kubernetes, SCOM, and Windows Server.

• Improve visibility, reliability, and operational efficiency by reducing alert noise, enhancing dashboards, and driving actionable insights.

• Define and promote standards for logging, metrics, dashboards, and alerting.

• Collaborate with engineering, platform, and security teams to ensure observability is embedded across solutions.

• Lead incident investigations, contribute to post-mortems, and turn lessons learned into platform improvements.

• Optimise platform performance, scalability, and cost.

• Share knowledge through documentation, best practices, and technical guidance across the organisation.

Your profile

You have 5+ years of experience in Software Engineering, Site Reliability Engineering, DevOps, Platform Engineering, or a similar role, with a strong focus on observability.

You bring hands-on experience with observability technologies such as:

• Metrics: Prometheus, Grafana, CloudWatch, Datadog, Dynatrace, New Relic, or similar.

• Logging: Elastic Stack, Splunk, Loki, Cloud Logging, or similar.

• Tracing: OpenTelemetry, Jaeger, Zipkin, X-Ray, or equivalent tracing solutions.

You also have experience with:

• SRE practices, including SLOs, SLIs, error budgets, and incident management.

• Distributed systems and cloud-native architectures.

• Operating and optimising Elastic Stack in production environments.

• Grafana and Kibana for dashboarding, visualisation, and alerting.

• Windows Server administration and monitoring, ideally including SCOM.

• Public cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP.

• Kubernetes, Docker, and container-based environments.

• Infrastructure-as-Code and CI/CD tooling (Terraform, Helm, CloudFormation, Pulumi, GitOps, etc.).

• Scripting or development experience in languages such as Java, Python, or Node.js.
